claude.sample_unit: people with type 2 diabetes and CKD

links.outcome: KFRE calibration on local historical data against ESKD endpoint
links.effect: Discrimination good (C-index 0.842 at 2y, 0.816 at 5y) but KFRE under-predicted ESKD risk overall and by ethnic group; underprediction larger at 5 years.
links.quote: Figure 2 suggests that the KFRE is underpredicting risks overall as well as in both ethnic groups ( online supplemental table S3 , online supplemental figure S4A ).

links.outcome: Effect of local recalibration on KFRE calibration metrics
links.effect: Recalibration using local cohort data improved ICI by more than 50%, E50 by more than 38% and E90 by more than 80% versus UK-recalibrated KFRE.
links.quote: Recalibration of the original KFRE performed far better than the KFRE (UK-recalibrated) with more than 50% improvement in ICI, more than 38% in E50 and more than 80% in E90 ( online supplemental table S6 and online supplemental figure S10 ).

links.outcome: KFRE discrimination and calibration across ethnic subgroups
links.effect: Discrimination unchanged in African Caribbean and Caucasian groups; underprediction in both, with 5-year E90 higher in Caucasian (0.078) than African Caribbean (0.057).
links.quote: These metrics are higher in Caucasian than in African Caribbean and particularly the E90 for 5 years (0.078, 95% CI 0.057 to 0.100 and 0.057 95% CI 0.036 to 0.078 for Caucasian and African Caribbean, respectively) ( online supplemental table S3 ).

links.outcome: KFRE calibration when applied to a new endpoint (ESKD) and population (T2DM with CKD)
links.effect: KFRE under-predicted ESKD risk; underprediction worse for eGFR<15 endpoint than eGFR<10, despite good discrimination (C-index 0.843 at 2y, 0.801 at 5y).
links.quote: With the threshold 15 mL/min defining the study event, we also observed an underprediction of the 2-year and 5-year risks, but it was more significant compared with what was found with the primary event definition ( table 2 and online supplemental figure S3 ).

models_evaluated: UK recalibrated four-variable Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE)
Original four-variable Kidney Failure Risk Equation (recalibrated to cohort)

links.effect: KFRE underpredicted ESKD risk; primary-endpoint C-index was 0.842 at 2 years and 0.816 at 5 years.
links.quote: We noted that KFRE ‘under-predicted’ the risk of ESKD in all the risk groups we defined by decile of 2-year and 5-year predicted risks suggesting a consistent pattern.

links.effect: Recalibration improved ICI >50%, E50 >38%, and E90 >80% versus UK-recalibrated KFRE.
links.quote: Recalibration of the original KFRE performed far better than the KFRE (UK-recalibrated) with more than 50% improvement in ICI, more than 38% in E50 and more than 80% in E90 ( online supplemental table S6 and online supplemental figure S10 ).

links.effect: 5-year E90 was 0.078 (95% CI 0.057 to 0.100) in Caucasian vs 0.057 (0.036 to 0.078) in African Caribbean.
links.quote: These metrics are higher in Caucasian than in African Caribbean and particularly the E90 for 5 years (0.078, 95% CI 0.057 to 0.100 and 0.057 95% CI 0.036 to 0.078 for Caucasian and African Caribbean, respectively) ( online supplemental table S3 ).

links.effect: Discrimination was adequate, but greater calibration was required for ESKD defined as sustained eGFR <10 or <15 mL/min/1.73 m2.
links.quote: Our observations suggest that although an adequate KFRE discrimination was obtained, greater calibration would be required for its application to predict ESKD whether defined as a sustained eGFR <10 or as a sustained eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m 2 .

links.effect: Recalibration improved ICI by >50%, E50 by >38%, and E90 by >80% compared with the UK-recalibrated KFRE.
links.quote: Recalibration of the original KFRE performed far better than the KFRE (UK-recalibrated) with more than 50% improvement in ICI, more than 38% in E50 and more than 80% in E90 ( online supplemental table S6 and online supplemental figure S10 ).

screen.reason: The study validates and recalibrates the Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE), a standard regression-based clinical risk equation rather than modern AI/machine learning, and does not evaluate clinical deployment or implementation safeguards.
